record.paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
record.original_question: Is there any natural computational problem, for example one arising in linear algebra, whose Weihrauch degree is AoUC⋄, where AoUC is the degree of finding a solution to bx = a with 0 ≤ a ≤ b?

evidence.quote: Let AoUC be the degree of finding a solution to bx = a where 0 ≤ a ≤ b
Open Question 14. Is there any natural problem (e.g. from linear algebra) in the Weihrauch degree AoUC⋄ ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Work in the framework of Weihrauch reducibility on multi-valued partial functions between represented spaces. For multi-valued problems f, g, write f ≤_W g for Weihrauch reducibility. Two problems are Weihrauch-equivalent (denoted ≡_W) if they reduce to each other; a Weihrauch degree is an equivalence class under ≡_W.

Define the problem AoUC ("All-or-Unique Choice on the unit interval") as follows: given a pair (a, b) of real numbers with 0 ≤ a ≤ b, AoUC outputs any real x satisfying b·x = a. (Equivalently, if b > 0 the unique solution x = a/b must be produced, and if b = 0 any real x is an admissible output.)

For a problem f, the diamond operator f^⋄ denotes the closure of f under finite (adaptively chosen) compositions: f^⋄ is, up to Weihrauch equivalence, the supremum of f, f ⋆ f, f ⋆ f ⋆ f, …, where ⋆ is the compositional product in the Weihrauch lattice. Thus AoUC^⋄ is the Weihrauch degree obtained by allowing finitely many adaptive applications of AoUC.

Problem.

Exhibit a "natural" computational problem — for instance, one arising from a standard question in linear algebra — whose Weihrauch degree is precisely AoUC^⋄, or prove that no such natural problem exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution identifying a natural (e.g. linear-algebraic) problem of Weihrauch degree exactly AoUC^⋄. Related work on AoUC and the diamond operator exists, but no source verifies a solution; status is therefore unclear from available evidence.

status_evidence.title: A note on the diamond operator - Linda Westrick
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the diamond operator on Weihrauch degrees, giving conditions under which f^⋄ ≤_W f.
status_evidence.claim: The diamond operator on Weihrauch degrees has been investigated, but the cited work does not identify a natural linear-algebra problem of degree AoUC^⋄.

status_evidence.title: An update on Weihrauch reducibility (and some open questions) – Pauly slides
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses AoUC and lists open questions about natural problems in various Weihrauch degrees.
status_evidence.claim: The question about a natural problem of degree AoUC^⋄ is listed among open questions; no resolution is reported.
